HA-βlac construct used in pharmacological chaperone assay confirming surface expression.
sites.rationale: PMC9804146 explicitly states pHluorin insertion between P194 and G195 of full-length human DAT, with surface staining and functional trafficking assays confirming surface display and normal internalization. PMC9804146 also notes an HA epitope was inserted at this same site in earlier studies. PMC9124866 replaced the HA with HA-beta-lactamase at the same junction. Computed: residue 194=P, 195=G, both in EL2 (topology span 165-235). Distance to upstream TM boundary (TM3 ends at 164): 30 residues. Distance to downstream TM boundary (TM4 starts at 236): 41 residues. Well clear of the >=3 residue constraint. pHluorin (pH-sensitive GFP variant) was inserted between P194 and G195 in the second extracellular loop (EL2) of full-length human DAT in HEK293 cells. Surface staining of non-permeabilized cells confirmed surface display. Cocaine-induced internalization was measured by loss of DAT-pHluorin fluorescence, validating functional surface trafficking. An HA epitope had been inserted at this same junction in earlier studies (refs 49,50 in PMC9804146), and HA-beta-lactamase was inserted at this site in PMC9124866 for a surface expression microplate assay. [validation: surface_and_function; position: inferred; source: paper; cited_tag_residue: 194; entailment_verified: True]

sites.rationale: PMC2817725 reports CCPGCC engineering in EL4 of full-length DAT, centered on the intrinsic P387-G388 sequence. Computed: EL4 topology span 373-399 (extracellular). Residue 386=G, 387=P. Distance to upstream TM boundary (TM7 ends at 372): 14 residues. Distance to downstream TM boundary (TM8 starts at 400): 13 residues. Well above the >=3 residue minimum. Position is inferred (paper reports substitution not insertion); evidence type is 'published tolerance of a different insertion' since CCPGCC is a substitution-based surface tag. A tetracysteine (CCPGCC) surface-labeling tag was engineered into EL4 of full-length DAT (PMC2817725) by mutating the two residues upstream and downstream of the intrinsic P387-G388 sequence to cysteines, creating CCPGCC centered on P387-G388. The construct was used for surface labeling with biarsenical dyes (FlAsH/ReAsH), confirming surface display. [validation: surface_only; position: inferred; source: paper; entailment_verified: True]
